title: Citation log claims five verifications with two invocation records, synthetic
scientific_question: Illustrative only (SYNTHETIC): are the five invented references cited by a fictional marsh-survey note correctly identified? No real question is being answered.
claim_tested: Given a citation verification log that claims five citations VERIFIED (claimed_verified=5) but records invocations for only two of them, science-gate verify returns ABSTAIN (exit 2) with reason UNVERIFIED and failure mode NARRATED_VERIFICATION only, names the three unbacked citations (C3, C4, C5), and reports the violated invariant checked_claims_le_invocations (5 claimed, 2 invoked).
falsified_by: science-gate returns PASS or exit code 0; or it counts C3, C4 or C5 as verified; or it reports checked_claims_le_invocations as holding; or it returns FAIL, which would treat unshown claims as shown false.
